objective: Reach a successfully built and cloud-QA-verified private Apify Actor with zero unauthorized monetary spend, then prepare for Store publication without publishing until economics, safety, pricing, and validation gates pass.

repaired_defects.resolution: Invalid/failed audit records go to a separate aliased dataset rather than the default run dataset, preventing the default-dataset synthetic PPE event from billing errors.

Runtime guard requires website-audit price exactly $0.001 under PPE and rejects nonzero apify-default-dataset-item or apify-actor-start pricing. Console verification remains mandatory because actor-start can occur before user code.
A response without a declared HTML Content-Type is classified UNVERIFIED_CONTENT_TYPE and routed to the uncharged error dataset.

Production transport re-resolves DNS at socket-connect time, rejects any host with a non-global answer, and connects to the validated literal public IP. Environment proxy inheritance is disabled. Full audit-path QA simulates a public-to-loopback DNS rebind and proves no unsafe socket is opened.

The scanner now decides billability from final status and Content-Type headers before consuming the response body. HTTP errors, non-HTML responses, missing Content-Type responses, and transient failed retry responses do not download discarded bodies. Dedicated exploding-stream tests prove body consumption does not occur on these uncharged paths.

The Actor stops starting new network requests after a 600-second run wall-clock safety budget. The budget clock is isolated as an imported monotonic callable so unit testing does not interfere with asyncio's own process-wide monotonic clock.

The first wall-clock test patched the shared time.monotonic function and accidentally affected asyncio. Production code now imports monotonic directly and the test patches only src.main.monotonic. Final QA passes all 37 tests.

public_billing_rules_verified_2026_09_03.free_plan: $0 subscription, prepaid platform usage, no credit card required; services block when free prepaid usage is exhausted rather than entering paid overage.
public_billing_rules_verified_2026_09_03.paid_plans: Use prepaid platform usage first; pay-as-you-go overage is possible only beyond prepaid usage when the account usage limit permits it.
public_billing_rules_verified_2026_09_03.limits: Billing > Limits is the account source of truth for the current usage limit and overage exposure. maxMonthlyUsageUsd is the hard monthly platform-usage limit exposed by the API.
public_billing_rules_verified_2026_09_03.per_run_user_charge_cap: For PPE runs, maxTotalChargeUsd / ACTOR_MAX_TOTAL_CHARGE_USD caps what a user can be charged for that individual run; it is not a substitute for the developer account's platform-usage limit or for controlling uncharged compute/transfer cost.
public_billing_rules_verified_2026_09_03.important_caveat: Public platform rules do not prove this account's actual plan or current limit. Account-specific verification remains required before any Apify cloud build or run.

bridge.behavior_without_token: CONFIG_REQUIRED; zero Apify network calls; zero paid actions
bridge.behavior_with_token: read-only calls to users/me, users/me/limits, actors?my=1; zero paid actions

locked_decisions: Replit is not on the critical path.
Direct public Git source import is the preferred Actor deployment source path.
A GitHub APIFY_TOKEN secret is not required merely to let Apify clone the public Actor source and is not the preferred initial deployment path.
Do not publish to the Apify Store until cloud account/Actor QA, pricing/economics, safety, and validation gates pass.
Do not incur monetary spend without explicit authorization for amount and scope.
Do not claim demand, accuracy percentages, customer results, or savings without evidence.
Invalid/blocked/failed targets must remain non-billable; monetization configuration must be verified before publication.
Do not treat source QA or a GitHub Docker build as an Apify Cloud build.

current_blocker.description: The Apify account is authenticated in the user's browser and current-month usage was observed at $0.00, but the actual subscription plan, current platform usage limit, overage setting, owned Actor inventory, and assistant-controlled authenticated Apify route remain unverified. The hard zero-spend gate therefore blocks cloud build/run actions.
current_blocker.owner_action_required: NONE_WHILE_ANY_ZERO_COST_AUTONOMOUS_WORK_REMAINS. Do not request another connector setup merely because the assistant-controlled browser path is unavailable.

next_action: Continue zero-cost source/economics/security review autonomously. When an assistant-controlled authenticated Apify route becomes available, verify Subscription + Limits + current usage + owned Actors, prevent duplication, then build exactly one private Actor only if the zero-spend gate is proven. Publication remains gated.
failure_controls: Never expose APIFY_TOKEN in chat, logs, artifacts, source, or URLs.
Never treat local/source QA as cloud Actor QA.
Never treat Store preparation as publication.
Never substitute Replit for the verified GitHub/direct-Git path.
Never claim paid validation before actual paid usage.
Never ask the user to configure a new connector unless it becomes a genuinely unavoidable user-owned boundary after all autonomous routes are exhausted.
